flags.title: $16.35/Hour Minimum Wage — Highest in Registry, Indexed to Inflation
flags.summary: $16.35/hr (2024), rising to $17.50 by 2026, then indexed to employment cost index — first state to fully index. CT Wage and Salary Act (WSA): 2-year SOL plus liquidated damages. CT Wage Theft Act (2022): criminal penalties. Always assess CT wage claims before defaulting to FLSA.

flags.title: Hartford — Highest Poverty Rate of Any State Capital (30%+)
flags.summary: Hartford poverty rate exceeds 30% — highest of any state capital. 40%+ Puerto Rican/Latino. Significant housing instability, high energy burden, food insecurity. CLS Hartford: 860-344-0380. InterCommunity Health Care FQHC: 860-569-5900. Charter Oak Health Center: 860-550-7500. Hartford just cause eviction ordinance applies within city.

flags.title: CHRO 300-Day SOL — Broadest Protected Classes in Region
flags.summary: CT Commission on Human Rights and Opportunities (CHRO) processes employment, housing, and public accommodation complaints with 300-day SOL matching EEOC. CFEPA protected classes: race, color, religion, national origin, sex, age, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, civil status, disability, and more. File CHRO AND EEOC simultaneously. CHRO: 860-541-3400.

flags.title: Mashantucket Pequot and Mohegan Tribes — Casino-Funded Tribal Infrastructure
flags.summary: Two federally recognized tribes with extensive casino revenue funding comprehensive tribal services. Mashantucket Pequot (Foxwoods): 860-396-6500 / mptn-nsn.gov. Mohegan Tribe (Mohegan Sun): 860-862-6100 / mohegan.com. Services: health, housing, education, elder care. Route enrolled members to tribal programs first. ICWA applies.

flags.title: Danbury — Dense Central American Immigrant Community, ICE Presence
flags.summary: Danbury (Fairfield County) has one of densest Guatemalan/Ecuadoran immigrant populations in Northeast (~40% Latin American). ICE operations have historically targeted Danbury area. Make the Road CT: 203-553-4340. CLS Danbury: 203-917-0141. HUSKY Health: undocumented adults emergency Medicaid only unless specific categorical eligibility.

flags.title: HUSKY Health (Medicaid) — Comprehensive Expansion Including Undocumented Children
flags.summary: HUSKY A (children/parents), B (CHIP), C (elderly/disabled), D (expanded adults 19-64 to 138% FPL; undocumented children CT-specific state-funded). Apply: AccessHealthCT.com or HUSKY directly. Managed Care: Aetna Better Health, Anthem BCBS CT, CHN, Wellcare. Phone: 877-284-8759.

flags.title: CT TFA (TANF) — 21-Month State Limit, Safety Net Program Available
flags.summary: Connecticut TFA (Temporary Family Assistance) has 21-month state lifetime limit — shorter than federal 60-month. After TFA exhausted, Safety Net program available. Screen for Safety Net BEFORE case closes. Never let TFA expire without assessing Safety Net eligibility. ~$698/month family of 3.

flags.title: Winter Shutoff Moratorium — November 1 to May 1
flags.summary: Connecticut winter shutoff moratorium: utilities cannot terminate service for low-income customers who enter payment arrangement from November 1 through May 1. Surface this protection prominently in any utility disconnection case during winter months.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Connecticut Emergency Certificate
flags.message: CT involuntary psychiatric hold law: Connecticut Emergency Certificate. Statutory authority: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 17a-502. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in CT retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in CT: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Connecticut Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Connecticut Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
